title: The Fragmented Future
spine: An explicitly imagined AI-assisted transit plan reveals both local capacity and external provider dependence; a river then crosses the political boundary, earning the book’s proposal for local choice combined with shared obligations and independent tools.

source.scope: Full 46-section map and complete prior 20-line film; complete sources3,4,5,8,14,33,35,37,43,44 read. This includes preface/methodology, map of futures, city-region, cosmolocalism, regional economy, fragmentation risks, constitution and conclusion. Not the full159k-character book or external references.
source.genre: Explicitly speculative nonfiction comparing political scales, historical analogies and alternative AI-era institutional designs.
source.images: Only source image is the cover, inspected. Its split utopian/dystopian city-tree scene is cover symbolism, not evidence or a body diagram. The original transit office and shared river-basin scenes replace icon geography with actual source-supported service/dependency functions.

scenes.title: Capability changes the scale
lines: The Fragmented Future asks what happens when AI changes the useful scale of government.
Small administrations may gain capabilities while larger authorities gain stronger tools of control.
This book compares those possibilities through history, political economy, and competing future scenarios.
It asks which decisions belong nearby, and which responsibilities must remain shared.
The aim is resilience through alternatives, rather than one prediction about tomorrow's political map.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Possibility begins with a useful local service, then widens into the question of who controls its capabilities.
scenes.artPlan: Use a lived metropolitan transit setting, not a geography of tiny house icons. A bus pulls into a sheltered stop with waiting adults, a driver and a clear destination; an adjoining modest planning room has two local staff examining the actual route. Expand the view to show the city depending on electricity and neighboring settlements beyond its administrative edge. Cobalt buses, coral shelter roofs, mint water, golden wayfinding and lilac civic clothing supply a bright, practical identity. One confident scene title. The scene is a hypothetical orientation rather than a claim about a real city or implemented AI service.

scenes.title: Who owns the useful service
lines: Imagine a city-region using AI to prepare a new bus route.
Local staff can compare travel needs without building a vast analytical department.
But the same provider might control the planning model, identities, and service access.
Apparent local independence can conceal dependence on an owner somewhere else.
The book treats that hidden control as part of the political arrangement.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Useful analytical help becomes unease when the same capability reaches a private dependency.
scenes.artPlan: Close into the actual route map and inhabit the planning room. An adult resident points to a stop near an existing cluster of homes; the assistant proposes a revised path, and the planner compares it with the original, rather than blindly approving it. Pull back to reveal the planning terminal and the resident service-login kiosk relying on the same external provider. In a visibly marked dependency test, that provider connection is unavailable: both terminals stop responding while the physical bus and people remain. The loss of access shows the dependence; a floating key or faceless block cannot substitute. No forced approval, instant transport improvement, actual named provider or claimed empirical failure. This is the source’s scenario mechanism applied to its explicit transit/planning functions.

scenes.title: The river crosses the boundary
lines: The boundary changes when consequences reach people beyond the city.
Water flowing downstream carries effects that a local vote cannot keep inside.
The proposed federation combines local experiments with shared rights, infrastructure, and obligations.
Wealthier regions cannot simply keep their advantages while abandoning the places supporting them.
Smaller government therefore earns its place by the problem it can responsibly handle.
scenes.emotionalPlan: The administrative map gives way to a shared physical consequence, then a reason to cooperate.
scenes.artPlan: Change to a wide inhabited river basin with upstream city, downstream settlement and a tributary. A clearly hypothetical rainfall pulse passes across a marked jurisdiction boundary toward both banks; no magical border stops the water. Do not invent deaths, flood probabilities, dam engineering or an instant protection result. Residents from the two places bring observations to a shared basin map while a common monitoring station remains visibly usable by both. A modest shared infrastructure contribution moves from the more developed city into monitoring/maintenance capacity used by both communities; avoid an invented monetary amount or finished flood defense. The contrast makes the book’s fiscal solidarity and cross-border responsibility concrete without assuming the smaller settlement is inherently incapable.

scenes.title: Keep another way to govern
lines: That argument leads to practical questions about replaceable services and independent scrutiny.
A public agency needs another way to work when its preferred system fails.
Critics also need tools that do not depend on the authority they challenge.
Begin with The Map of Possible Futures, then test the Constitution of Resilience.
Read the darker scenarios alongside those proposals to see which freedoms each arrangement risks.
This is a book for comparing political designs before one becomes difficult to escape.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Release comes from preserving alternatives and a clear reading route, not a utopian victory.
scenes.artPlan: Return to the disrupted transit office at a different close scale. A printed route and documented independent terminal provide a degraded fallback, while the resident keeps the same request; service can continue in a limited way without pretending every normal function is restored. A civic reviewer uses a separately supplied tool to inspect the original and proposed routes; the executive’s preferred model cannot also provide the only criticism. Keep the review open. End with the physical book on the route table, opened to the two actual chapter destinations, beside the retained original route. This illustrates proposed infrastructure pluralism and epistemic separation, not a vendor product demonstration or a guarantee of political freedom.

evidence.heading: PREFACE
evidence.quote: The technologies that make some forms of centralization less necessary may also make centralization more powerful.

evidence.heading: METHODOLOGICAL NOTE
evidence.quote: This is a work of disciplined speculation.

evidence.heading: PREFACE
evidence.quote: History provides analogies but not laws.

evidence.heading: THE MAP OF POSSIBLE FUTURES
evidence.quote: The central proposition of this book can be stated in one sentence: artificial intelligence may make smaller political units more administratively viable at the same time that it makes very large political units more powerful.

evidence.heading: THE MAP OF POSSIBLE FUTURES
evidence.quote: One company may provide the personal agent, identity layer, payment system, work marketplace, education, health navigation, insurance, reputation, and communication.

evidence.heading: THE RETURN OF THE CITY-REGION
evidence.quote: AI may lower the threshold further by providing legal, planning, translation, and analytical capacity to regions that previously lacked it.

evidence.heading: THE RETURN OF THE CITY-REGION
evidence.quote: Wastewater may require a watershed authority. Transit may need a metropolitan region.

evidence.heading: THE RETURN OF THE CITY-REGION
evidence.quote: If the same official model writes the proposal, summarizes criticism, predicts impacts, and recommends the final choice, participation becomes ceremonial.

evidence.heading: THE RETURN OF THE CITY-REGION
evidence.quote: Local democracy in the AI era therefore requires epistemic separation: opposition, media, civil society, universities, and courts need independent cognitive tools.

evidence.heading: THE POLITICAL ECONOMY OF THE CITY-REGION
evidence.quote: Conversely, a rich region that keeps all locally generated revenue while benefiting from a common market, defense, currency, universities, migration, and national infrastructure is not autonomous so much as subsidized by the larger system.

evidence.heading: THE POLITICAL ECONOMY OF THE CITY-REGION
evidence.quote: A federation pools those risks.

evidence.heading: THE DARK SIDE OF FRAGMENTATION
evidence.quote: The owner may never use spectacular coercion because dependency does the work.

evidence.heading: THE DARK SIDE OF FRAGMENTATION
evidence.quote: Rivers, air basins, forests, grids, coastlines, and migration corridors cross local boundaries.

evidence.heading: THE DARK SIDE OF FRAGMENTATION
evidence.quote: Polycentric environmental governance works when overlapping authorities can negotiate and when higher levels can act against persistent externalization.

evidence.heading: A CONSTITUTION OF RESILIENCE
evidence.quote: Functions are assigned according to externality, required scale, and the value of local knowledge.

evidence.heading: A CONSTITUTION OF RESILIENCE
evidence.quote: Critical public functions should have substitutable providers, multiple implementations, offline or degraded modes, and documented exit plans.

evidence.heading: A CONSTITUTION OF RESILIENCE
evidence.quote: Institutions that decide, execute, prosecute, judge, inform, and audit should not depend completely on the same model or data pipeline.

evidence.heading: A CONSTITUTION OF RESILIENCE
evidence.quote: A common standard should not require one product.

evidence.heading: CONCLUSION
evidence.quote: The deepest case for fragmentation is epistemic humility.

evidence.heading: CONCLUSION
evidence.quote: The deepest case for federation is moral and strategic realism.

technicalBoundaries: Transit/connection failure and river-basin scenes are explicitly hypothetical illustrations, not named historical events or empirical forecasts.
An AI route is proposed and compared, not automatically safe, fair, implemented or superior.
No claim that smaller government is naturally democratic or that states necessarily disappear.
The outside provider’s unavailable connection illustrates dependence without alleging misconduct by a real company.
No invented catastrophe, hydrological quantity, flood-defense design or immediate guarantee of safety.
Fallback service is partial and proposed; independent review remains unresolved.
Common rights, fiscal solidarity and shared infrastructure remain substantive conditions of the preferred scenario.
supersedesDefects: Prior island/workshop/key arrangements never showed the administrative function AI cheapens or the outside service controlling it.
The more concrete storm idea is retained as an inhabited cross-boundary basin rather than an ornamental threat icon.
